review.rationale: The exact native entry identifies additive coordination of clauses. That compositional relation connects its operands independently of whether either operand describes desire or refusal. Desire introduced by a coordinated clause belongs to that clause, not to this additive connector. WANT=0 is supported by the identified function, not by the empty primitives map.

The native entry explicitly identifies a declarative complement link. It can link a content clause to a desire predicate or a non-desire predicate without changing this lexical use. Wanting belongs to the governing predicate or the content clause; complement linkage itself is orthogonal to wanting. This judgment is confined to the conjunction entry, not the demonstrative spelling.

The native entry specifies indefinite singular determination. Selecting a singular indefinite nominal reference does not assert that an experiencer wants or does not want it. A desire for the referent must be supplied by the containing predicate. This explicit reference function supports WANT=0; the missing bank declaration alone would not.

The native entry specifies definite determination. Identifiability of the nominal referent is independent of an experiencer favoring or refusing that referent. The definite-reference contribution supports WANT=0 for this entry; no conclusion is drawn about desire expressed elsewhere in a sentence.

The native entry specifies a possessive relation. A possession or association relation does not assert wanting to obtain, keep, or avoid either participant. Those attitudes would require additional lexical content. WANT=0 is justified for this exact possessive relational use; no HAVE or other-bank ruling is being made.

The native feature is specifically spatial_type=GOAL. A destination relation is not itself a mental desire or an absence/refusal of desire; something can move to a destination without any wanting being asserted. WANT=0 applies to this spatial-goal preposition entry, not every infinitival, purposive, or idiomatic use of the spelling to.

The exact source declares SOMETHING with third-person singular neuter reference. The pronoun identifies a referent; it does not predicate that the referent or speaker wants something. Grammatical INANIMATE is not being projected to NOT WANT. Reference itself is orthogonal to the wanting coordinate, supporting explicit 0 for this entry.

The exact source declares SOMETHING with distal singular deixis. Distal identification supplies which referent is indicated, not an attitude of wanting or refusing it. Desiring a distal object is separate predicate content. WANT=0 is supported for this demonstrative pronoun use only.

The source declares SOMETHING and marks its grammatical use interrogative. This identifies the queried entity slot; a speaker's wish to know an answer is a possible speech-act interpretation, not the slot's own lexical desire component. Under the existing word/grammar boundary, this exact pronoun use is orthogonal to WANT. This does not set sentence-level questioning or intention to zero.

The exact native row declares SOMEONE with second-person nominative reference. It identifies the addressee independently of that person's present wants or refusals. Being an animate person capable of wanting is not an assertion of lexical WANT. Explicit 0 is supported for this reference use. Earlier model-valued banks in this receipt are not used as justification or retrospectively approved.

The complete native leaf identifies the name of Latin U/u; its linked forms and spelling examples support that letter-name sense rather than the second-person pronoun. Naming a letter is not a desire or a refusal. WANT=0 follows from this identified lexical sense, not the noun category or its previous model zeros. Those older model rulings remain unreviewed here.

The exact synset defines the ninth Roman-alphabet letter and traces ancestry through letter, character, written symbol and communication. This lexical object identifies a symbol, not an experiencer's desire concerning it. WANT=0 is supported for this letter sense; no evidence is transferred from first-person I.

The complete definition and explicit chemical-element/halogen ancestry identify iodine. Its listed applications and occurrence describe uses and physical occurrence, not a lexical attitude of wanting or refusing. A person may desire iodine, but that external relation is not the chemical-element meaning. WANT=0 is supported for this exact synset, not by an assumption that all substances or nouns receive zero.

The exact definition fixes a length unit equal to one twelfth of a foot, with linear-unit and measurement ancestry. That metrological identity does not predicate desire or refusal by an experiencer. WANT=0 is supported for this unit sense; the prepositional spelling in is not being substituted for the definition.

The complete gloss and knowledge-domain/engineering ancestry identify the discipline concerned with computer and telecommunications information handling. The functions retrieve, store and transmit describe its technical subject matter. They do not lexically assert a particular experiencer's desire or refusal. WANT=0 is supported for this discipline sense; human purposes motivating its practice are separate from this definition's own attitude content.

The exact synset and administrative-district/state ancestry identify Maine in New England. Geographic or administrative identification does not encode an experiencer's desire or refusal. WANT=0 is supported for this named-state sense, without importing first-person me or claims about what residents want. This review does not decide whether geographic facts should remain in the corpus.
